extracted.intended_audience: Proposers preparing DARPA Other Transactions (OT) proposals — universities, industry teams, researchers, and prime/subawardees
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting proposals in response to DARPA Broad Agency Announcements when requesting Research or Prototype Other Transactions, including required forms, milestone content, IP assertions, and research-security obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestone content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposers requesting an OT must include a detailed list of milestones. Each milestone must include the following: milestone description, completion criteria, due date, and payment/funding schedule (to include, if cost share is proposed, awardee and Government share amounts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a minimum, milestones should relate directly to accomplishment of program technical metrics as defined in the BAA and/or the proposer’s proposal. Milestone agreement type (fixed flexible or fixed-price based) will be subject to negotiation by the Agreements Officer. Milestone templates available in Attachment 3 - Schedule of Milestones and Payments Templates (Fixed Flexible | Fixed Price Based). Do not include proprietary data in milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on proprietary data in proposal milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include proprietary data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit admonition repeated in Milestone Schedule Instructions — proprietary data should not be included in milestone submissions or associated schedule attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of DARPA-specific Representations and Certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposers are required to submit for all award instrument types supplementary DARPA-specific representations and certifications at the time of proposal submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Reps and Certs page for further information on required representations and certifications depending on your requested award instrument. Failure to provide required reps and certs can render the proposal non-conforming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost sharing / matching disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If cost share is proposed, include awardee and Government share amounts in the payment/funding schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For more information on Cost Sharing/Matching requirements for Other Transactions for Prototype and Research, see Acquisition Innovation. Cost share details should be included in milestone payment schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property and data rights assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers shall appropriately identify any potential restrictions on the Government’s use of any Intellectual Property contemplated under the award instrument in question, including both Noncommercial Items and Commercial Items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no restrictions are intended, the proposer should state “NONE.” The prime proposer is responsible for compiling all data rights assertions, including those of any subcontractors. Proposers are encouraged to use a format similar to the template provided on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: IP assertion template fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Template fields for asserting restrictions on technical data / computer software to be furnished with restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested fields: Summary of Intended Use in the Conduct of the Research (NARRATIVE); Basis for Assertion (LIST); Asserted Rights Category (LIST); Name of Person Asserting Restrictions (LIST). Use these headings to clearly present asserted restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental research declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers should indicate in their proposal whether they believe the scope of the research included in their proposal is fundamental or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While proposers should clearly explain intended research results, the Government has sole discretion to determine whether proposed research is fundamental and to select the award instrument type. Appropriate language will be included in awards for non-fundamental research to prescribe publication requirements and other restrictions. Proposers must explain which efforts are fundamental and why (including when subawardees differ). See DARPA link on Fundamental Research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with DoD/ OUSD(R&E) risk-based security review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers must comply with DoD policy directing components to establish risk-based security review programs to identify and mitigate undue foreign influence consistent with NSPM-33 and OUSD(R&E) guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, proposers must follow the June 8, 2023 OUSD(R&E) 'Policy on Risk-Based Security Reviews on Fundamental Research' and the updated '2025 DoD Component Decision Matrix to Inform Fundamental Research Proposal Mitigation Decisions' (May 5, 2025). DARPA will assess Covered Individuals using Common Disclosure Forms and compare potential risk factors to the DoD Risk Decision Matrix to determine mitigation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish internal processes for research security and foreign talent issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The performer or recipient must establish and maintain an internal process or procedure to address malign foreign talent programs, conflicts of commitment, conflicts of interest, and research integrity consistent with USD(R&E) direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performers must utilize due diligence to identify Foreign Components or participation by Covered Individuals in Foreign Government Talent Recruitment Programs and agree to share such information with the Government upon request. This requirement must be flowed down to subtier performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Common Disclosure Forms and digital persistent identifiers (DPIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key personnel named in OT proposals are required to submit Common Disclosure Forms in the approved format, and provide a digital persistent identifier (DPI), prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD Grant Information Notice 24-01 requires use of the Common Form for Biographical Sketch and Common Form for Current and Pending (Other) Support for assistance awards; these requirements are applied to OTs for R&D. Effective 1 April 2025, DoD must use DPIs and DARPA will require ORCID numbers for each covered person listed in a proposal for non-FAR based award instruments. Forms and detailed instructions are on NSF.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirements for Covered Individuals and key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers must submit Form 1 (Common Form for Biographical Sketch) and Form 2 (Common Form for Current and Pending (Other) Support) for all covered individuals and for all other key personnel, regardless of proposal submission method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 1 (Biographical Sketch) is mandatory for Project Directors (PD) and Principal Investigators (PI), and designated covered individuals; optional but desired for other key personnel. Biographical sketch should include: Identifying Information (ORCID DPI), Position Title, Organization and Location, Professional Preparation (education and training), Appointments and Positions, Products, Certification. Form 2 (Current and Pending) is mandatory for all covered individuals: it includes Proposals and Active Projects (Source of Support; Primary Place of Performance; Active Project Start/End Date; Total Anticipated Project Amount; Person-Month(s) per year; Overall Objectives; Statement of Potential Overlap) and In-Kind Contributions (Status; Receipt Date; Source; Summary; Person-Months; USD Value; Objectives; Statement of Potential Overlap), plus Certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to update covered-individual status and obtain approval for changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes to covered individuals will require submission of the Common Disclosure Forms, a security-based risk assessment, and approval by the contracting officer and program manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The above-described information must be provided as part of the proposal and will be reviewed utilizing a risk-based security review process prior to award. DARPA will assess entirety of Common Disclosure Forms and publicly available validation sources against the DoD Risk Decision Matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources and factors used in DARPA risk-based security reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: DARPA’s risk-based security review process takes into consideration the entirety of the Covered Individual’s Common Disclosure Forms and leverages publicly available lists or reports to identify potential risk factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists and reports include, but are not limited to: FY22 Lists Published in Response to Section 1286 of the NDAA for FY 2019; Executive Order 13959; U.S. Dept. of Commerce BIS List of Parties of Concern; DNI Annual Threat Assessment (2025); DCSA products regarding targeting of U.S. technologies and exploitation of academia. These will be compared to the DoD Risk Decision Matrix to determine mitigation or denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited foreign-influence conditions that may require denial
rubrics_metrics.description: The DoD has explicitly stated certain foreign influence risks are not able to be mitigated and would require denial of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples called out: (1) Beginning in FY2024, no U.S. Institution of Higher Learning that hosts a Confucius Institute may receive DoD funding unless issued a waiver under Section 1062 of the FY2021 NDAA; such institutions are automatically classified as 'prohibited'. (2) As of Aug 9, 2024, DoD is prohibited from funding a fundamental research project proposal in which a Covered Individual participates in a Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment Program (MFTRP) or to an institution that does not have a policy addressing MFTRP; such individuals and institutions are automatically classified as 'prohibited' under OUSD(R&E) policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and disclosure obligations during performance
rubrics_metrics.description: If, at any time during performance, the performer or recipient learns that it, its Covered Individuals, or applicable team members are or are believed to be participants in a malign foreign government talent program or exhibiting behaviors identified by the DoD Decision Matrix, the performer must notify the Government Contracting Officer or Agreements Officer within 5 business days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure must include specific information about personnel involved and the nature of the relationship. The Government will have 30 business days to review and may conduct fact-finding. Disclosure may lead to termination of the award. If no response from the Government within 30 business days, the University may presume the Government has determined the disclosure does not represent a threat. This provision must be flowed down to any subtier contracts or agreements involving direct participation in performance of the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title VI non-discrimination compliance in DARPA assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: DARPA’s analysis and assessment of affiliations and associations of Covered Individuals is compliant with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964; information regarding race, color, or national origin is not collected and does not have bearing in DARPA’s assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performers with proposals selected for negotiation that have been assessed as having potential undue foreign influence risk factors may be given an opportunity during negotiation to mitigate the risk; DARPA reserves the right to request follow-up information to assess potential risk factors or proposed mitigation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for missing required security or proposal information
rubrics_metrics.description: If DARPA receives a proposal without the required information, DARPA may determine that the proposal is non-conforming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A non-conforming determination could result in elimination from further review and consideration under the solicitation. DARPA reserves the right to request further details from the proposer before making a final funding determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: University Ph.D. student/post-doctoral researcher continuity funding conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a DARPA-funded program awarded through a Research or Prototype OT where a University participates ends before planned program completion (due to termination or down-select), DARPA may continue to fund, for no more than two semesters (or equivalent), the documented costs to employ or sponsor Ph.D. students and/or post-doctoral researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government will notify the University via Agreements Office or prime performer. The University must: make reasonable efforts to find alternative research or employment for the students/researchers; submit documentation describing due diligence certified by a University official; affected students/researchers must submit statements of work describing research activities during the funded period and the final deliverable. DARPA will rely on information from the University's original proposal unless updated proposals are warranted. No funding will be provided if the program ended due to suspected or actual fraud or negligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: DARPA down-select and phased-award process considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: DARPA often structures programs in phases or options that include specific objectives and a designated period of performance; this may result in issuing multiple awards to maximize innovative approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advancement to subsequent phases or exercise of a planned option will be based, at a minimum, on stated evaluation criteria, metrics, funding availability, and program goals and objectives. This structure allows Government monitoring and programmatic decision points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-on production eligibility under 10 U.S.C. § 4022(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government may award a follow-on production contract or Other Transaction for any OT awarded under this solicitation if certain statutory conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: (1) the participant (or recognized successor in interest) successfully completed the entire prototype project provided for in the OT, as modified; and (2) the OT provides for the award of a follow-on production contract or OT to the participant or recognized successor in interest.
